newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay to cut 70 jobs at Belgian plant.
newsitem.headline: Solvay to cut 70 jobs at Belgian plant.

text.p: Belgian chemicals group Solvay SA said on Thursday that 70 jobs would be lost at its Jemeppes-sur-Sambre PVC plant in Belgium's Namur province as a result of a restructuring to boost competitiveness.
"It's true that there will be about 70 job losses, but only by early retirement at age 55. There will be no other redundancies," Solvay spokesman Jean Lampe told Reuters.
Lampe was responding to union fears about the future of the plant, which the socialist union FGTB's Francy Careme said now employed 1,150 staff from 2,500 at its opening 32 years ago.

In a letter to Solvay chairman Daniel Janssen, the union voiced its concern about the future of the company's 19,000 Belgian employees following last month's 14 billion francs sale of Solvay's animal health businesses and what the FGTB described as the closure of PVC production at Jemeppes.

Lampe said restructuring at Jemeppes was needed given the highly competitive PVC market and high Belgian labour costs. But he said Solvay had no plans to close the plant, in which more than 10 billion francs was invested over the past 10 years.
"We have not abandoned the Jemeppes plant, but we must recognise economic realities," said Lampe.
